label: TP
reason: The CodeQL report identifies two sources reaching the XSS sink via string concatenation. Source 1 is getValue() on cookieValue which comes from request.getCookies(), and Source 2 is getName() on the same Cookie objects. While these are technically server-side generated strings based on request parameters passed during initialization, they represent untrusted data flowing directly into the response stream without encoding, meeting the definition of a cross-site scripting vulnerability on the reported path.

evidence.note: Cookie values and names concatenate directly into response output without HTML encoding
